M1.title: Preparing for the search
M1.subtitle: Recognising ignorance, waking inquiry, preparing the mind with discernment and dispassion

M2.title: Understanding and self-examination
M2.subtitle: Listening, examining, abiding — and turning from the seen toward the witness

M3.title: From experience to the experiencer
M3.subtitle: Experience, the one who experiences, ‘Who am I?’ — and the one reality of all

M4.title: From silence to natural living
M4.subtitle: The limit of knowing, silence, and an ordinary life settled in understanding

weeks.theme: The difference between the seen and the seer
weeks.pointer: This week, pause three times a day and look: what is being seen, and to whom.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: At which moment was this distinction clearest, and when was it most blurred?

weeks.pointer: Thoughts are not to be stopped. Each thought is to be known as it comes and goes.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: Was there a thought that felt like ‘I’? How did you see it?

weeks.pointer: Feel the feeling fully, and see where the ‘I’ joins in ‘I am sad’.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: What was the strongest feeling this week? How did ‘I’ attach to it?

weeks.pointer: While working, see: is the sense ‘I am doing’ there every moment, or does it come and go as well?
weeks.reflectionPrompt: In which task was the burden of doership heaviest, and in which lightest?

weeks.pointer: Watch every experience come and go — and also that which does not go.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: Did you try to hold on to or repeat an experience?

weeks.pointer: See the very sense ‘it is happening to me’ as an experience.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: What happened when you looked at the experiencer?

weeks.pointer: The witness is not to be searched for; see in what everything is appearing. Keep an eye on the pride of ‘I am the witness’ too.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: Did ‘the witness’ ever start becoming a new identity?

weeks.pointer: Notice the ‘I’ behind each thought — when it rises, and when it does not.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: What was there in the moments without the ‘I’-thought?

weeks.pointer: A few minutes daily: to whom? — to me. — who am I? Without making an answer.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: What changed this week with ‘Who am I?’

weeks.pointer: Take the reactions that rise in relationships as the laboratory of understanding.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: Write one reaction in full: what happened, what rose, what was seen.

weeks.pointer: Recognise, between sounds and thoughts, the background in which they appear.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: Was silence seen even while sound was there?

weeks.pointer: Drop the effort to do anything special. Live an ordinary day with understanding.
weeks.reflectionPrompt: How has the way you see life changed in these twelve weeks?

prompts: How do you see experience and the experiencer now?
When a strong reaction arises, where do you find the ‘I’?
How has the question ‘Who am I?’ changed for you compared with the beginning?
What do you see now about your deepest identity, the one you used to take as ‘I’?
Where do you recognise witnessing in your daily life — and where does it become a new belief?
What is silence for you now?
Which doubt still remains? Write it honestly.
How does understanding show in relationships and work — and where does it not?
What did you gain on this journey — or did the very idea of ‘gaining’ change?

terms.gloss: Ajñāna — not knowing one's own nature; not a lack of information, a mistaken identity.
Jijñāsā — a true longing to know the truth, which turns back on the one who asks.
Viveka — the clarity that distinguishes the lasting from the passing, and the seer from the seen.
Vairāgya — inner freedom from clinging; not escape or suppression.
Śravaṇa — listening to the teaching attentively, again and again, as being about oneself.
Manana — reflecting on the teaching heard, until doubt ends.
Nididhyāsana — abiding deeply in the understood truth, so that it becomes natural.
Neti-neti — ‘not this, not this’: the method of removing mistaken identities.
Sākṣībhāva — the awareness in which everything appears; not a thought, not coldness.
Anubhava — experience: what appears, and goes.
Anubhavakartā — the experiencer: the sense that calls every experience ‘mine’, which is itself known.
Ātma-vicāra — self-inquiry: turning attention back to the source of ‘I’ — ‘Who am I?’
Ātma-jñāna — recognising one's own ever-present nature; not a new experience or an achievement.
Brahma-jñāna — knowing the one reality of all names and forms as one's own nature.
Ajñeyatā — the knower cannot become an object of knowledge; not ignorance.
Śūnyatā — empty of objects, not of awareness.
Mauna — silence: the background of sound and thought; not mere quiet.
Sthitaprajña — one whose understanding is steady; who lives in equanimity.
Sahaja — an ordinary, natural life settled in understanding — nothing to gain, become or drop.
